frontMatter.title: The Scoreboard: All 101 Languages Ranked
frontMatter.description: Every score in the 101-language comparison in one place — the ranked table, the six Core, eight Ecosystem, and six Readiness dimension sub-scores, and the complete per-language mechanism data behind each number.

frontMatterLines: description: Every score in the 101-language comparison in one place — the ranked table, the six Core, eight Ecosystem, and six Readiness dimension sub-scores, and the complete per-language mechanism data behind each number.

blocks.q: **Companion to:** [The Great Language Smackdown](index.qmd) · [the Criteria](scoring-criteria.qmd) · [the Scoring Model](objective-coupling-scoring-model.qmd)

blocks.p: This page holds every number in the comparison. Every table responds to the controls above it: type to filter, and choose a key to re-rank. The first table ranks all 101 languages by the **ranking score** — coupling, lifted by at most 15% for readiness — with the star band that follows from Core coupling, and shows Ecosystem coupling alongside. The next three give the per-dimension sub-scores that produce those totals. The last table gives the mechanism-presence data behind every score, so any number can be reproduced from first principles. The criteria are on [the Criteria](scoring-criteria.qmd); the arithmetic, the presence rules, and the ranking rule are on [the Scoring Model](objective-coupling-scoring-model.qmd).
How each language constrains the six Core coupling dimensions. The leading column is the score; the rest are the per-dimension costs that produce it.

*Higher is better for the score column. Every (cost) column is a cost in score points, where 0 means the language forces no mechanism in that dimension. Analysis date: October 2026. The 'Platform' column is the language's platform/domain coupling.*

**The leading column is a score; the rest are costs.** A dimension carries a cost in score points: `0` means the language forces no mechanism in that dimension, and a negative number is the dimension's share of the axis inventory. The cost is `100 × raw ÷ inventory weight`, and the raw weight sum follows in parentheses, so the mechanism inventory stays checkable. Each cell is rounded for display and the axis total is computed from the integer raw sums, so a column can differ from its total by a few tenths.

ul: 0 = the type states the meaning of every value. A cost = producers and consumers must agree on meaning that nothing records.
0 = state is local by default and every value passes a validating path. A cost = state leaks into globals, or values arise without validation.
0 = the language states when storage is released and who owns it. A cost = the program must hold that answer in convention, not in the language.
0 = failures travel a declared path and force a decision. A cost = failures travel by side channel, and nobody must handle them.
0 = parallel work is expressible and kept off shared state. A cost = shared state is the default, and races go undetected.
0 = the artifact runs beyond one vendor or domain. A cost = the deployment unit is a single vendor, domain, or dead platform.

blocks.p: How each language handles ecosystem-level coupling. The leading column is the axis score; the rest are the per-dimension costs that produce it.

**The leading column is a score; the rest are costs.** A dimension carries a cost in score points: `0` means the language forces no mechanism in that dimension, and a negative number is the dimension's share of the axis inventory. The cost is `100 × raw ÷ inventory weight`, and the raw weight sum follows in parentheses, so the mechanism inventory stays checkable. Each cell is rounded for display and the axis total is computed from the integer raw sums, so a column can differ from its total by a few tenths.

ul: 0 = predictable, deterministic performance. A cost = GC pauses, warm-up, or interpretation couple logic to the runtime.
0 = standardized tooling and a rich ecosystem. A cost = fragmented or thin tooling couples the project to its toolchain.
0 = stable and backward compatible. A cost = breaking changes couple the codebase to a version.
0 = works across domains. A cost = coupled to one domain, or to one framework's architecture.
0 = quick to productivity. A cost = productivity couples to deep, unusual expertise.
0 = concise and readable. A cost = verbosity or inconsistency couples intent to ceremony.
0 = strong tools and early detection. A cost = poor tools couple understanding to manual inspection.
0 = memory- and type-safe. A cost = correctness couples to security awareness.

blocks.p: How each language builds reproducibly, ships verifiably, can be observed, is quick to work in, connects to other languages, and is governed. Higher is better; the score is reported separately from the two coupling scores.

**The leading column is a score; the rest are costs.** A dimension carries a cost in score points: `0` means the language forces no mechanism in that dimension, and a negative number is the dimension's share of the axis inventory. The cost is `100 × raw ÷ inventory weight`, and the raw weight sum follows in parentheses, so the mechanism inventory stays checkable. Each cell is rounded for display and the axis total is computed from the integer raw sums, so a column can differ from its total by a few tenths.

ul: 0 = the artifact rebuilds byte-identically and dependencies are pinned. A cost = the build or its dependency graph is not reproducible.
0 = published packages carry provenance and live in a namespaced registry. A cost = origin is trusted rather than verified.
0 = traces, metrics, and structured logs are standard. A cost = a running program cannot be observed with standard tooling.
0 = the edit-build-test loop is short and the editor answers as you type. A cost = a change pays a long rebuild, or the editor cannot answer.
0 = the language calls other languages and compiles to a portable target. A cost = it is an island.
0 = an independent body or an open specification owns the language. A cost = one vendor, or a closed specification, does.
